title: First fast.2 integration: controlled native timing and accuracy evidence

units.cpu_s: process CPU seconds summed over threads

notes: All 34 controlled-native reports, the earlier W1 baseline profile, and both final 19-case audits are retained. No spectra or input sample arrays are included.

Raw-source paths are repository-relative identifiers for the untracked source reports. SHA256 values identify the exact raw files used; this curated dataset contains the retained measurements even without those files.
The file-mtime range is filesystem metadata, not an independent measurement-clock record. Exact audit creation timestamps are copied from their JSON reports.
API timers exclude imports, input generation, warm-up, fingerprints, and file output. Warm-up and setup times are retained separately.
RSS is a process-lifetime high-water mark. The 4096 MiB working budget controls admission of concurrent work and is not a hard process-RSS cap.
The earlier W1 baseline used an automatic budget; controlled-native runs explicitly use 4096 MiB. W1 phase comparisons change version, kernel, and outputs together.

Profile child phases subdivide parent phases. Do not add C preparation/segments to C kernel time, or window generation/sums to window_and_sums time. Length-band sums are derived from the raw frequency rows.
The first fast.2 native build used GCC 13.3.0 with -march=native. These measurements do not establish the performance of portable wheels or ARM/Apple builds.

Some environment records retain installed-distribution metadata naming fast.1 while the loaded lpsd_fast module is fast.2. Loaded-module metadata and binary/source fingerprints identify the measured implementation.

A robust PSD-only wall-time advantage was not demonstrated: all three alternating W8 pairs were slower for PSD-only, and W1 ranges overlap. Do not attribute whole-version speedups solely to output selection.

Boxcar regressed in the observed 1M medians: auto/all was about 24.3% slower and fast/PSD about 33.5% slower than fast.1. Other tested windows improved; no universal window-speedup claim is supported.
Accuracy uses the unchanged scalar path with an independent original-C anchor. Relative maxima and every at-or-above-limit count remain visible.

Combined acceptance is relative error strictly below 1% OR absolute error at most the explicitly supplied allowance. PSD=1e-24 and NSD=1e-12 apply to these fixed synthetic amplitudes and units; neither is a default for arbitrary signals.
The HFT248D on-bin cases and the larger off-bin case retain relative violations. Their combined acceptance must not be described as passing a universal relative 1% bound.
Output SHA256 values are reproducibility fingerprints, not a substitute for the separate numerical audit. No runtime accuracy fallback was used.
Later optional Kaiser power-series results belong to a separate dataset and must not be mixed with this c41db40c build.

Accuracy case parameters inherit n/sample_rate/n_frequencies/n_averages from their audit configuration. frequency_sha256 is shared by the exactly matching reference/candidate grids; all output arrays are float32.

Per-metric diagnostic_points de-duplicate maxima and exceptional points using roles. Arbitrary maximum locations for zero-error arrays are omitted; maxima, counts, statuses, and output hashes are retained. Per-density limits are stored once in each audit.

baseline_fast1_native.limitation: Baseline reports contain no build sidecar or at-measurement binary hash. The current baseline binary was fingerprinted after measurement; compiler identity comes from its ELF comment. Flags are reconstructed from the pinned builder and the coordinator-reported native build mode, not recovered from a compiler-command log.

output_selection_n10000000_w1.interpretation: Three repeats per variant have overlapping ranges; these runs do not establish a robust PSD-only speedup.
